q8.answer: The merge reads staging through a select that keeps only the highest updated_at per order_id, and MERGE updates a matching warehouse row only when src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at. So an older copy never overwrites a newer one, and re-merging an identical version changes nothing.

q9.answer: It is stored in etl.control (one row per pipeline, column high_water_mark) and nowhere else. The value written is the attempt's cutoff, but only if it is larger than the current value. It is written inside the same warehouse transaction as the merge, so it moves at commit time and never on failure.

q10.answer: wh.orders is the only table dashboards read, and it is changed only by the single merge transaction. A 06:00 refresh therefore sees the whole night or none of it. Staging is a separate table that dashboards never read.

q11.answer: Each attempt empties etl.stg_orders before loading, so the failed attempt's staged rows are deleted (attempts run one at a time, so nothing else uses it). The HWM was not changed by the failure, so the retry reads the same HWM, uses lower = HWM - 2h, and takes a fresh cutoff from the replica.

q12.answer: It re-reads every row created on each mismatched day (by created_at) from the replica, not just rows in the nightly window. It empties staging, loads them tagged with the reconcile run_id, and merges all mismatched days into wh.orders in one transaction using the same >= rule, then deletes the run's staging rows. It does not touch the nightly HWM.
